task371-leipzig-drone:0.claim_text: Last year, a Chinese woman was convicted for passing on information about flight schedules and cargo movements at Leipzig/Halle Airport to a man spying for Beijing.
Last year, a Chinese national was convicted for passing information about flight schedules and cargo movements at Leipzig/Halle airport to a man spying for Beijing.

task371-leipzig-drone:1.claim_text: The tabloid Bild speculated that the explosive device could have been fabricated from fertiliser and petrol.
Public broadcasters NDR and WDR, as well as the Süddeutsche newspaper, said the device contained pentaerythritol tetranitrate (PETN), a primary ingredient in semtex.
German media reported that the attached bomb was made of PETN and semtex plastic explosive.

task371-leipzig-drone:2.claim_text: Russian secret services were reportedly plotting an attack against Stefan Thumann, the head of German drone manufacturer Donaustahl.

German investigators were tipped off by a foreign intelligence service at the end of last year and arrested a Ukrainian man and a Romanian woman this spring related to the plotting against Stefan Thumann.
Stefan Thumann is said to be under police protection due to the plot.
A pan-European investigation identified 22 suspects in Lithuania and Poland suspected of being employed by Russian intelligence.

task371-leipzig-drone:3.claim_text: In 2024, US intelligence services reportedly foiled a Russian plot to assassinate Armin Papperger, chief executive of Germany’s leading arms manufacturer Rheinmetall.
The plot to murder Armin Papperger was reportedly one of several Russian government schemes targeting defense industry executives in Europe supporting Ukraine’s war effort.
The assassination plot against Armin Papperger was believed to be the most advanced among the reported Russian schemes.

task371-leipzig-drone:4.claim_text: NATO jets struggled to shoot down incoming drones during the first drone incursion case, with most drones eventually crashing or losing power and gliding to the ground.
Western militaries struggled to identify the perpetrators and respond promptly to the surveillance drones in the second incursion case.

task371-leipzig-drone:5.claim_text: A second firebomb package traveled to the UK and caught fire at a warehouse in Birmingham.
Two similar firebomb packages were found in Poland.

task371-leipzig-drone:6.claim_text: Police and prosecutors said there is no danger to the lives or safety of passengers or airport staff, and passenger air traffic is unaffected.
There was no danger to passengers or airport employees during the incident, and flights were not affected during the day.

task371-leipzig-drone:7.claim_text: The parcel fires in July 2024 targeted the UK and EU countries and are suspected to be sabotage linked to Moscow.
Russia has denied involvement in the parcel fires targeting the UK and EU countries.

task371-leipzig-drone:8.claim_text: Germany’s interior minister Alexander Dobrindt said the incident did not appear to be the work of amateurs.
Alexander Dobrindt and other German officials did not explicitly mention Russia as a potential suspect in their remarks.

task371-leipzig-drone:9.claim_text: German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt described the incidents as a professional, hybrid threat scenario.
Alexander Dobrindt said investigators were treating the drone incident as part of a professional hybrid threat scenario.
Alexander Dobrindt described the incident as a hybrid attack scenario.

task371-leipzig-drone:10.claim_text: Alexander Dobrindt suggested the investigation may point to a possible competition that may involve foreign powers.
Alexander Dobrindt said there might be foreign powers involved in the drone incident aiming to contribute to considerable uncertainty in Germany.

task371-leipzig-drone:11.claim_text: In July 2024, a parcel burst into flames on the ground at Leipzig/Halle Airport before it could be loaded onto a DHL cargo plane.
A firebomb exploded at Leipzig airport in July 2024, posted via DHL.

task371-leipzig-drone:12.claim_text: The second unidentified object landed in Hanover with minor damage to the cargo aircraft.
Minor damage was detected on the cargo aircraft after the collision, which later landed in Hanover.

task371-leipzig-drone:13.claim_text: The initial evidence points firmly towards a Russian-orchestrated plot for the drone incident.
Details about the explosives, the origin of the drone, and who was behind the incident are under ongoing investigation.

task371-leipzig-drone:14.claim_text: A second unidentified object collided with a cargo aircraft near Leipzig/Halle Airport.
A DHL cargo plane aborted its landing at Leipzig airport and collided with an unknown object in mid-air as it climbed away from the airport.
A suspected second unidentified flying object collided with a cargo aircraft after it had taken off following the previous closure of the runway at Leipzig airport.
A second unidentified flying object, possibly another drone, collided with a DHL cargo plane several hundred metres above the ground after the first incident.
An apparent second flying object collided with a freight airplane after it aborted a landing at Leipzig/Halle because the runway was closed.

task371-leipzig-drone:15.claim_text: The DHL cargo plane later landed safely elsewhere after the collision.
The DHL cargo plane only sustained minor damage from the collision with the unidentified flying object.

task371-leipzig-drone:16.claim_text: Russia has not commented on the drone incidents at Leipzig/Halle Airport.
Moscow has not commented on the drone incident so far.

task371-leipzig-drone:17.claim_text: Leipzig/Halle Airport is used by the German military and NATO allies for transport of military goods.
Leipzig/Halle Airport serves as a base for Ukraine's Antonov Airlines which carry most of Ukraine's aerial cargo.
Leipzig airport is a NATO and German military logistics hub and is the base for Ukraine’s Antonov Airlines in Europe.
Leipzig airport is the European base of Ukrainian Antonov jets used for heavy cargo.
Leipzig airport is used by NATO and the German military for transport.

task371-leipzig-drone:18.claim_text: Leipzig/Halle Airport is a major hub for the logistics group DHL.
Leipzig airport is a DHL hub.

task371-leipzig-drone:19.claim_text: German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said that the drone carrying explosives represents a new quality of danger.
A drone armed with explosives at an airport is a new threat scenario, according to German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt.

task371-leipzig-drone:20.claim_text: German airports are on high alert following several unauthorized drone flights in recent months over military bases, airports, energy terminals, seaports and logistics companies.
Similar incidents with suspicious drones in Germany have only happened since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
Germany and other European countries have experienced a series of suspicious unauthorized drone overflights at airports, military facilities, ports, and logistics companies.

task371-leipzig-drone:21.claim_text: Ukraine's Ambassador to Germany Oleksii Makeiev stated that Russia could be responsible for the drone incidents.
The airport’s status as a NATO and German military hub and base for Ukraine’s Antonov Airlines has directed suspicion toward Russia regarding the drone incident.
Ukraine’s ambassador to Germany Oleksii Makeiev blamed Moscow for the drone incident.

task371-leipzig-drone:22.claim_text: Police have warned of a potential Russian involvement in the drone incidents, which Moscow has denied.
Russia has previously been accused of carrying out sabotage attacks in Europe.
Germany and other European countries have accused Russian agents of being behind some unauthorized drone flights, which Moscow has denied.
Germany has accused Russia of orchestrating a campaign of sabotage, espionage, and disinformation against it, which the Kremlin has denied.

task371-leipzig-drone:23.claim_text: The detonator was removed from the explosive device and police later carried out a controlled explosion at Leipzig/Halle Airport.
The bomb attached to the drone did not explode because the detonator was faulty.
Police removed the detonator from the drone with the explosive device.

task371-leipzig-drone:24.claim_text: A NATO official said they are aware of the drone incident at Leipzig airport and that investigations continue.
NATO was aware of the drone incident at Leipzig airport on Wednesday.

task371-leipzig-drone:25.claim_text: German police deployed a bomb disposal robot to defuse and destroy the explosive device found at Leipzig airport.
Police deployed a bomb disposal robot to examine the drone at Leipzig airport.

task371-leipzig-drone:26.claim_text: A robot was deployed at Leipzig/Halle Airport after the explosive device was spotted by an employee near Ukrainian cargo planes overnight.
An anti-explosives robot was deployed to check an object near the south runway at Leipzig/Halle Airport.

task371-leipzig-drone:27.claim_text: Flights on the northern runway at Leipzig/Halle Airport resumed at 01:55 (23:55 GMT on Tuesday).
The southern runway at Leipzig/Halle Airport remains closed.
Operations in the northern part of Leipzig airport resumed two hours after the incident.
Both the runways at Leipzig/Halle Airport were closed after a flying object was sighted nearby shortly before midnight Tuesday.
The north runway at Leipzig/Halle Airport was reopened after about two hours.

task371-leipzig-drone:28.claim_text: The drone found near a Ukrainian Antonov cargo plane was a quadcopter fitted with an explosive device.
Photographs published by German newspapers show a quadcopter drone with a package attached near a Ukrainian Antonov cargo plane.

task371-leipzig-drone:29.claim_text: A drone carrying an explosive device has been found at Leipzig/Halle Airport in Germany.
The explosive-laden drone was spotted close to parked Antonov planes at Leipzig/Halle Airport.
A small drone carrying explosives was discovered at Leipzig airport on Wednesday morning.
Investigators said a drone carrying an unknown explosive device was spotted by an airport employee near the south runway of Leipzig airport.
The southern runway of Leipzig airport, where the drone was found, remained closed after the incident.
An armed drone was found at Leipzig airport on Wednesday.
The drone was carrying an unknown explosive device when discovered in the secure cargo flight operations area near the airport’s southern runway.
Police discovered as much as 800 grams of explosive on the drone at Leipzig airport.
A drone with explosives was found at Germany's Leipzig/Halle Airport and the device was defused.
An airport employee discovered a drone near the airport's south runway with an unknown explosive device.

task371-leipzig-drone:30.claim_text: The discovery of the drone caused flight diversions at Leipzig airport.
Several aircraft, including a passenger plane from Mallorca, were diverted because of the drone incident at Leipzig airport.
